name: connect-other-ais
description: Your AI writes the code; other vendors' models review it — the plan before it is built, the diff after. A gate that holds until they agree, or until you decide.

coai.promptsPerRound.markdownDescription: Which prompt each role uses on each round, by catalog id — `{ "Architecture": ["architecture", "arch-boundaries"] }`. Index 0 is round 1. An empty or unknown entry is treated as *not chosen*: round 1 of a code role falls back to the conventions pass when the repository has written rules, and every other round to that role's universal prompt.

coai.onExhausted.markdownDescription: When rounds run out with findings still gating: `continue` as-is (said out loud), call a `human`, or `escalate` the ladder (reviewer effort → reviewer model → arbiter model).

coai.maxConcurrency.description: Reviewer CLI processes running at once, machine-wide.

coai.maxPerProvider.description: Reviewer CLI processes per vendor at once — a rate limit is per vendor.

coai.roundTimeoutMinutes.markdownDescription: How long a **whole round** may take before the reviewers still running are cancelled and the round is gated on whatever answered. `0` works it out from the round itself — vendors × roles reviewers through the concurrency cap, each wave allowed one reviewer timeout. At the defaults that is four waves: forty minutes. Lowering it cuts into reviewers that have not finished; their findings are lost.

coai.credsKey.markdownDescription: The CredsForDevs **config-entry key** (minted by *Enable Code Access…* on the entry holding vendor API keys). A pass to one vault entry — revocable, useless while VS Code is closed — not a secret itself. Empty = keyless vendors only.

coai.escalationMinutes.description: How long a question waits for you before the AI is told to ask in the chat instead.

coai.teamServers.markdownDescription: Team servers — one company subscription per vendor, running the CLIs on one machine. Add them in the **ConnectOtherAIs** panel; signing in uses your work Microsoft account and the token is kept in a file only you can read, never here.

id.description: Generated once when the server is added, and never rewritten — reviewer rows are named after it, so changing it would orphan them and their spending history.

name.description: What you call it. Display only; safe to change.

url.description: Its address. https, or http only on this machine.

coai.vendors.markdownDescription: The reviewers. Edit them in the **ConnectOtherAIs** panel — add a vendor, remove one, or point it at another model. `runtime` is which CLI shape it uses (`codex` or `gemini`); `baseUrl` makes it an OpenAI-compatible endpoint driven through the Codex CLI.

id.description: Short name; also names its key in the vault entry.

remoteVendor.description: For a Team server reviewer: the vendor id THAT SERVER knows it by, which is not this row's id.

model.description: Empty uses the CLI's own default.

baseUrl.description: OpenAI-compatible endpoint, for a vendor riding the Codex CLI.

coai.rounds.markdownDescription: How many rounds each reviewer ROLE gets. Architecture may be worth two passes with different lenses while performance is worth one; a shared budget forces the cheapest role to pay for the most expensive. Edit it in the **ConnectOtherAIs** panel.

coai.roleEnabled.markdownDescription: Which CODE-review roles take part. Unticking one means that role does not take part in the round at all — no reviewer is launched for it and its findings count towards nothing. Its rounds, threshold and prompts are kept and come back unchanged when it is ticked again. Plan review is not affected.

coai.thresholds.markdownDescription: How many blocking/major findings each ROLE may still have and pass. A finding is counted against the threshold of the role that raised it.

coai.dealPlanLenses.markdownDescription: Deal the plan stage’s lenses across the vendors instead of giving every vendor the same one. **Off** (the default): every vendor answers the same question, so two vendors agreeing on a finding is a fact the gate can use. **On**: every lens gets asked once at half the launches, and that agreement is gone.

coai.dealCodeLenses.markdownDescription: Deal the three code roles across the vendors, one vendor each, instead of asking every role of every vendor.

enumDescriptions: Fast — the reviewer gets the diff, the plan and the project's rules, in an empty directory.
Full — the reviewer also gets the checkout of the commit under review.
coai.codeWorkspace.markdownDescription: What a code reviewer is given. **Fast** (default) sends the composed prompt with nothing to explore; measured, every hosted model found more useful defects that way at a fraction of the input tokens. **Full** also hands it the checkout of the commit under review.

coai.uiScale.markdownDescription: Text size on the ConnectOtherAIs help page, in steps of 10% from the base — `5` is about ×1.6, `-5` about ÷1.6. The ± buttons on the page write this same setting, and it syncs with your other machines.

coai.helpLanguage.markdownDescription: The language of the **Help** pages only. Articles not yet translated show English with a note. The switch at the top of the help page writes this same setting.

coai.perSideSettings.markdownDescription: Keep **separate settings for each side of this machine** — a local window, and each WSL distro or remote host on its own. Off (the default) is one set of settings for every window, exactly as before. On, each side keeps its own values, seeded from what it had at the moment you switched it on, so nothing changes until you edit something. For one person working for several companies on one machine: a different proxy (`baseUrl`), a different CLI path and a different vault key per side. Does **not** separate `uiScale` or `helpLanguage` — a text size belongs to you, not to the company. Stored in the extension's own state, not in `settings.json`, because VS Code hands one `settings.json` to every extension host.

coai.autonomous.markdownDescription: Tell the assistant to work autonomously: questions that do not block are collected and asked at the END, all together; one that does block is asked at once, but only after every other blocking question it can foresee has been gathered, so you are interrupted once.

coai.splitPlan.markdownDescription: After a plan passes, tell the assistant to break it into 2-4 epics and each into 2-4 logically complete stories, and to close every story properly: review its diff through this gate, fix, document, test, commit. The order is given once per assistant — an epic coming back for its own review is told it is a piece, not told to split again.

coai.splitWithFable.markdownDescription: Do the split itself with Fable at its highest version, and send the stories where being wrong is expensive — payments, security, architecture, data migration — back to it; the ordinary ones run on Opus. Fable here is a model of YOUR assistant, not a reviewer in the list.

coai.chatPrompt.markdownDescription: **Replaced by `#coai.chatPromptPresets#`.** What a captured passage used to be sent with. It is read once, to carry what you had written into your first named preset, and nothing reads it after that — so edit the presets instead. It stays here for one release so that upgrade cannot lose the prompt you wrote.

coai.chatPromptPresets.markdownDescription: Your saved prompts, each with a name. One is the MAIN one — the one used when a capture sends by itself (see `#coai.chatAutoSend#`). Edit them in **ConnectOtherAIs: Edit chat presets**, which is easier than editing this. A row needs a `name` and a `text`; anything else in it is ignored, and a row missing either is dropped rather than taking the list with it.

coai.chatModelPresets.markdownDescription: Your saved models, each with a name and optionally a prompt the composer opens with. `provider` is the reviewer ROW that answers — the same identity the picker stores — and `model` is which of its models, or empty for whatever that row is set to. Edit them in **ConnectOtherAIs: Edit chat presets**.

coai.chatLanguage.markdownDescription: The language the OTHER AI answers a chat in. Deliberately not `#coai.helpLanguage#`: the help pages and the explanations are two different audiences, and one setting cannot answer both.

enumDescriptions: The keybinding sends; the right-click menu fills the box and waits.
Neither sends — the passage always lands in the box for you to send.
coai.chatAutoSend.markdownDescription:
Whether a captured passage is asked immediately, or put in the box for you to send.

The default spends a vendor turn automatically ONLY where the text is certainly the passage you just selected — the keybinding copies it itself. The right-click menu takes whatever is on the clipboard and cannot know how old that is, so it fills the box instead.

coai.chatModel.markdownDescription: Which configured reviewer answers a chat, by its id. Empty means the first one that can — today that is any row on the `antigravity` runtime.

scripts.test: node --test scripts/prepare-gate.test.mjs && npm run compile && node scripts/run-tests.mjs
scripts.package: npm run test && npm run bundle && vsce package --no-dependencies
